description:
Runs the maintenance checks across every site in a portfolio and returns one report
ordered by what needs action first: what is down, what expires soonest, what regressed
since the last run.

Use it to answer "what needs attention this week?", "is anything down?" or "what do I put
in this quarter's report?" across a whole client list. It is the right call whenever the
question is about more than one site — running domain_check, ssl_check and uptime_check
once per site by hand is what this replaces.

The portfolio comes from the "sites" argument, or from a local JSON file ("sites.json" by
default) whose format is documented in sites.example.json. Pass "checks" to override what
each site asks for — ["uptime"] answers "is anything down right now?" in a fraction of the
time — and "tags" or "client" to report on part of the portfolio.

For a document a client will read, pass "format": "markdown", with "client" for one
client's sites: it is in plain language, says what needs a decision from them, and reads the
same way every quarter. Add your own narrative around it rather than rewriting its dates and
counts. "csv" gives a spreadsheet, "ical" a renewal calendar to import, and "concise" a short
result for a large portfolio.

Do not use it to answer a question about one site: domain_check, ssl_check, uptime_check
and seo_audit answer those directly and in a fraction of the time. It runs checks and
reports; it never changes a site, and it never writes to the portfolio file.

A site that cannot be checked is reported as a finding, never as a failure of the whole
report. Only a portfolio that cannot be read at all is an error.

What changed since the previous run is compared against one recorded snapshot. For a
portfolio file that snapshot lives in memory by default and is lost when this server
restarts; the file may add a "history" path, and then the snapshot is written there and
comparisons survive a restart for up to 100 days. Nothing is written unless the portfolio
asks for it. Sites passed inline keep no history at all, so that no caller is ever compared
against another's run: compare them with "includeSnapshot" and "baselineSnapshot". Either way
the report says what it had to compare against, and why it had nothing when it had nothing,
rather than implying nothing changed. Sites are compared only on the checks both runs
measured, so a quick uptime-only pass never invents regressions in the run after it, and
it does not replace what a wider run recorded: other checks keep their last result, and a
"tags" or "client" run leaves the sites it filtered out as they were.

For a quarterly report, compare against a moment you chose rather than the last run: save a
run with "saveBaselineAs" and compare with "baselineName" (needs a "history" path), or ask
for "includeSnapshot" and pass the result back as "baselineSnapshot" (works everywhere,
including a hosted instance, which stores nothing). Changes then list what was resolved,
what is new and what is still open since that moment.

baselineName.description: Compare against the baseline saved under this name instead of against the last run, e.g. "2026-Q3". Use it for a quarterly report, so that weekly runs in between do not move what the quarter is compared with. Needs a portfolio file with a "history" path; otherwise use "baselineSnapshot".

baselineSnapshot.description: A "snapshot" returned by an earlier report, passed back unchanged, to compare against. Takes precedence over "baselineName". Refused if it was altered, or is over 400 days old.

checks.description: Run exactly these checks for every site, ignoring what the file says. Use it for a quick pass — ["uptime"] answers "is anything down right now?" in a fraction of the time.

client.description: Only report on the sites of this client, e.g. "Example Bakery Ltd", as named by each site's "client" field. Matched case-insensitively. Use it to produce one client's report.

file.description: Path to a portfolio JSON file, e.g. "/Users/you/sites.json". Give the full path: a relative one is resolved against the directory this server was started in, which for a desktop client is usually "/" and not the user's own. Defaults to "sites.json". Ignored when "sites" is given. The format is documented in sites.example.json; only .json files can be read.

format.description: What the text of the result holds. "full", the default, is the report for whoever maintains the sites. "markdown" is a document for the client, in plain language, ready to paste: use it, with "client", for a client report. "csv" is one row per finding, for a spreadsheet. "ical" is a renewal calendar to import: every domain, and certificates within 30 days; what has already expired, or has no known date, is listed beside it instead. "concise" is the summary alone and also leaves each site's findings and checks out of the structured result, for a large portfolio where the full result would be too long.

includeSnapshot.description: Return this run as "snapshot", for the caller to keep and pass back next quarter as "baselineSnapshot". This is how to compare across quarters with no history file, and the only way on a hosted instance, which stores nothing. It names the sites, so keep it as carefully as the portfolio. A check that could not run this time keeps what the last run, or the snapshot passed back, found for it, dated when it was found.

saveBaselineAs.description: Also save this run as a baseline under this name, e.g. "2026-Q4". A full run replaces one of the same name, and a run filtered by "client" or "tags" adds its sites to it, so a quarter can be saved one client at a time. A check that could not run keeps what the last run found for it. Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, 40 at most. Needs a portfolio file with a "history" path; otherwise use "includeSnapshot".

sites.description: The portfolio, passed inline, 200 sites at most. Use this for a one-off report over a handful of sites. An inline portfolio keeps no history between calls, so to say what changed pass "includeSnapshot" now and "baselineSnapshot" next time. When omitted, the portfolio is read from the local file instead.

checks.description: Which checks to run for this site. Defaults to domain, ssl and uptime.

client.description: Who this site belongs to, e.g. "Example Bakery Ltd", for reporting per client.

domain.description: Registrable domain for registration and DNS checks, e.g. "example.com". Derived from the URL when omitted; set it when the site lives on a subdomain. A bare public suffix such as "co.uk" is refused.

expiryWarningDays.description: Warn this many days before the domain registration expires, e.g. 60. Defaults to 30. Also sets when the renewal reminder in the iCal calendar fires for the domain. It does not change certificate warnings: those follow each certificate's own lifetime (14 days ahead for a 90-day certificate).

maxLinks.description: Internal links the seo check may request for this site, 0 to check none. Defaults to 25. This is what a portfolio run spends its time on: one request per link, paced at half a second per host, so twenty-five links is roughly twelve seconds for that site.

name.description: Human label used in the report, e.g. "Example Bakery".

notes.description: Context carried through into the report.

tags.description: Free-form labels, for filtering a report.

url.description: The address a visitor would use, e.g. "https://www.example.com". Scheme optional.

tags.description: Only report on sites carrying at least one of these tags, e.g. ["retainer"]. Matched case-insensitively. Omit to report on the whole portfolio.

name: portfolio_report

changes.description: What changed since the run this one was compared against.

comparedAgainst.description: What this run was compared with.

comparedWithPreviousRun.description: False when there was no usable previous run, in which case nothing can be said about what changed. Read "previousRunUnavailable" for why.

findingsPastTheWindow.description: Findings that could not be measured again for so long that they are past the window a comparison uses (100 days, or 400 for a baseline), so they are no longer compared: neither resolved nor still open. Check them by hand.

lastMeasuredAt.description: When it was last actually measured.

historyKeptIn.description: Where this portfolio's history is kept: the path of the history file, "memory" when a portfolio file names none, or "nowhere" for sites passed inline, which keep none so that no caller is compared against another's run. Memory is lost on restart; a portfolio file may add a "history" path to compare across restarts.

from.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

to.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

newFindings.description: Findings that were not present in the previous run.

newSites.description: The sites counted in sitesNewSincePreviousRun, by name. What they found is in their own entries: none of it is "new" in newFindings, which compares like with like.

persistingFindings.description: Findings present in both: what is still open from last time.

previousRunUnavailable.description: Why there was no previous run to compare against, e.g. "there is no history file at /Users/you/upkeep-history.json yet, so this run creates one". Null when there was one — including when there was one and no site turned out comparable, which the counts below explain instead.

regressed.description: Sites that got worse since the previous run.

from.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

to.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

resolvedFindings.description: Findings the compared run had and this one does not: what got fixed. `actionable` says whether it was a warning or worse, rather than an informational line.

sitesCompared.description: How many sites this run could actually be compared against, on the checks both runs measured: comparing a quick uptime-only pass with a full run on anything else would invent regressions, or hide them.

sitesDroppedSinceBaseline.description: Sites the compared run checked that this one did not, with the findings worth acting on they last had. Always empty for a "tags" or "client" report, which leaves sites out on purpose.

sitesMeasuredDifferently.description: Sites the previous run also checked, but with no check in common, so they were not compared. Two full runs back to back compare everything.

sitesNewSincePreviousRun.description: Sites the previous run did not check at all, so there is nothing to compare.

sitesNotMeasured.description: Sites where no check could run this time, so there is nothing to compare yet.

sitesPartlyCompared.description: Sites among those compared where only some checks could be: a check failed this time, or only one of the runs made it. What those checks found is neither new nor resolved.

sitesPastTheWindow.description: Sites whose earlier results were all too old to compare against.

unmeasuredFindings.description: Findings the compared run had that this run could not measure again, e.g. an expiring domain when the registry did not answer: neither resolved nor confirmed.

file.description: The file it was read from, when it was read from one.

generatedAt.description: When the report was produced, ISO 8601 in UTC.

needsAttention.description: Everything worth acting on, worst first. This is the list the report exists to produce.

needsClient.description: Whether acting on it needs the client: money, a decision, or access only they hold.

plain.description: The same finding in plain language, for someone who does not maintain the site. Worded the same way every time.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

notes.description: Anything the report could not do, said plainly rather than left out.

savedBaseline.description: The name this run was saved under, when it was asked to be and could be.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

siteCount.description: How many sites the report covers, after any tag filter.

checks.description: One entry per check that was asked for.

error.description: Why the check could not run, when it could not. Null otherwise.

ran.description: False when the check could not run at all.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

unmeasured.description: Finding codes this check ran but could not establish either way, e.g. "domain_expires_soon" when the registry did not answer; a trailing * covers a prefix, and "*" alone means the check examined nothing, e.g. a page robots.txt kept it out of.

client.description: Who this site belongs to, when the portfolio says.

domain.description: The registrable domain that was checked.

findings.description: Everything found for this site, worst first, each tagged with the check.

code.description: Stable identifier for this kind of observation, e.g. "cert_expires_soon".

message.description: One sentence explaining the observation in plain words.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

name.description: The site as named in the portfolio.

notes.description: Whatever the portfolio file said about this site.

renewals.description: Everything found on this site with an expiry date.

remindDaysBefore.description: Days ahead the iCal reminder fires: the site's expiryWarningDays for a domain, 7 for a certificate.

subject.description: The domain or host it belongs to.

severity.description: How much attention this needs. "critical" means act now; "warning" means act this month; "unknown" means the check could not establish the fact, which is not the same as it being fine.

soonestExpiryDays.description: Days until the first thing about this site expires — registration or certificate, whichever is sooner. Null when nothing with a date could be read.

tags.description: The tags this site carries in the portfolio file.

snapshot.description: This run, for passing back later as "baselineSnapshot". Null unless "includeSnapshot" was set. It names the sites.

summary.description: How many sites landed at each severity.

title: Whole portfolio, ranked by urgency
